title: Gifting Money to NRI Child: TCS on LRS & Refund Explained
description: Gifting money to an NRI child from a resident Indian parent is tax-free for the recipient in India. Remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) .

faq.q: Is a gift from a parent to an NRI child taxable in India?
faq.a: No, a gift of money from a parent to an NRI child is exempt from income tax in India for the child, as gifts from specified relatives are not considered taxable income under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: What is the LRS limit for gifting money abroad?
faq.a: Resident Indians can remit up to USD 250,000 (approximately ₹2 crores) per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) for various permissible purposes, including gifts.

faq.q: What is the TCS rate on gifting money to an NRI child?
faq.a: For financial year 2025-26 onwards, a 20% TCS is applicable on gift remittances exceeding ₹10 lakhs in a financial year, on the amount above this threshold.

faq.q: Does TCS apply if I transfer money to my NRI child's NRO account in India?
faq.a: Generally, no. Transfers from a resident Indian's account to an NRI's NRO account within India for gifting purposes are typically not subject to TCS as per prevailing banking practice.

faq.q: Can I get a refund for the TCS paid on a gift remittance?
faq.a: Yes, the TCS collected is an advance tax. The remitter (parent) can claim this amount as a credit against their income tax liability or seek a refund when filing their Income Tax Return in India.

faq.q: What if the gift is for education or medical treatment?
faq.a: Remittances for education (self-funded) or medical treatment are subject to a lower TCS rate of 2% on amounts exceeding ₹10 lakhs, from FY 2025-26 onwards. If education is funded by an approved loan, TCS is 0%. It's crucial to use the correct purpose code.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate and comprehensive overview of gifting money to an NRI child, covering LRS, TCS, and refund mechanisms, with correct references to relevant sections of the Income Tax Act and RBI regulations. However, there are some discrepancies regarding the effective dates and specific TCS rates for certain categories, particularly for FY 2025-26 vs. FY 2026-27.
